messages.author: 49a67c6e0f03dace
messages.subject: QTL effect p value
parts:
Hello Carl,

I'm using the fitqtl to extract the QTL effects, and I would like to see whether the phenotype mean values for different genotypes at the locus with the highest LOD (from a significant QTL) are significantly different (like a t test). I would like to see the p value. Do you think I can use the t value in the output from estimated effect table? Is this t value the t test value? I can't find the explanation of this value in the help...

If I can't use any value from the results, how can I pull out the genotypes (with imputation genotypes) for a specific loci?

Thanks!

Ziming

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] QTL effect p value
parts:
The LOD score is equivalent to a t-test. The approach we take for p-values is to use a permutation test, particularly so that we can then adjust for the scan across the genome. And so I would focus on genome-scan-adjusted p-values that you can get from the scanone summary.

the t-value with estimated effects in fitqtl() would just be estimate / SE, and the p-values do not adjust for the genome scan. I ignore those p-values completely.

karl
